fatal_blockers: Ideas 1, 2, and 7 share one provable soundness hole: they amplify only the clause-residual vector r, but with integer slack variables (or non-Boolean integer assignments) every 3-CNF affine clause equation can be zeroed exactly, so a cheater sets r=0 and pays only an O(1) un-amplified anchoring penalty per non-Boolean coordinate. The gap is then 1+O(1/sqrt(n0)), not D^{(K-1)/(2K)}; RS spreading, field norms, and CRT blocks all amplify a quantity the adversary can make identically zero. Unless a mutation makes the Booleanity/anchoring cost itself amplify, all three die on paper before any experiment.

Idea 1's asymptotic claim also collides with a known complexity ceiling: GapCVP with factor sqrt(n/log n) is in NP∩coNP (Aharonov–Regev 2005) and in coAM (Goldreich–Goldwasser 2000), so exponents approaching 1/2 as K grows would imply a collapse. Any surviving mutation must target a fixed small c, and the write-up's 'polynomial gap for large K' framing is inadmissible as stated.

Idea 3 is not currently a reduction at all: Plücker/Segre minor constraints are quadratic in lattice coefficients, while CVP admits only linear integer combinations under a quadratic norm, and the proposal concedes no linear realization is known. Standard linearization reintroduces exactly the product-consistency variables it was meant to constrain, recursively.

Idea 5 requires polynomial-size compression of Nullstellensatz certificates whose degree/size are known to be exponential in the worst case (Boolean Nullstellensatz degree lower bounds, e.g. Grigoriev-style; Brownawell/Kollár bounds are doubly exponential-free but still huge); assuming such compression is an unproved conjecture, which the campaign brief forbids. Small-n Gröbner experiments cannot certify the asymptotic compression claim.

Idea 6 is blocked by treewidth: exact contraction of a general 3-CNF clause tensor network in polynomial bond dimension would compute the SAT partition function in polynomial time, which the mechanism itself would need before any lattice gadget exists. The proposal admits this; no bounded experiment escapes it.

Idea 4's obstruction class over Z is computable in polynomial time via Smith normal form, so hardness must be relocated into 'nearest integral chain' geometry — which is itself a CVP instance, making the route circular unless the systolic-product support lower bound does independent work; that bound is currently unstated and unproved.
evidence: The supplied obstruction map (IDEAS.md, STATUS.md) is genuinely empty and no verifier evidence or experiment logs exist; therefore every 'expected move' in pro_ideas.md is an unverified claim and none may be promoted. All soundness assessments above are paper-level, consistent with the ORACLE_BRIEF requirement that soundness be attacked by executable searches before promotion.

The non-Boolean cheat against Ideas 1/2/7 is checkable by hand on the proposal's own toy instance: for (x)∧(¬x) with residuals (x−1,x) no cheat exists, but the toy is unrepresentative because real 3-CNF clauses need slacks (x+y+z−1−s=0 with free integer s), which zero all residuals for arbitrary integer assignments. The proposals' smallest experiments omit or under-specify slack handling, so as written they would produce misleadingly positive results.

Aharonov–Regev (STOC/JACM 2005) and Goldreich–Goldwasser (JCSS 2000) are classical, pre-dating any off-limits material, and cap the achievable exponent at c<1/2 absent NP=coNP; this must be added to the obstruction map as a proved ceiling.
No search results describing the prohibited document were consulted; this review uses only classical literature and the supplied files.
next_experiment: One bounded experiment testing the shared soundness assumption of Ideas 1/2/7 with slacks made explicit: encode a minimal unsatisfiable 3-CNF (e.g. all eight clauses on x,y,z or (x)∧(¬x) with genuine 3-literal padding and integer slack lattice directions), build the RS-amplified lattice with N=64 evaluation points and per-coordinate Boolean anchors on variables AND slacks, then exhaustively enumerate integer assignments/slacks in [−20,20] and report min cheating distance versus the claimed Omega(sqrt(N)) soundness bound. Expected outcome: cheating distance within O(1) of the completeness distance, which kills Ideas 1, 2, and 7 jointly and seeds the obstruction map with 'residual-amplification without amplified Booleanity is void'; if instead the gap survives, the anchoring mechanism deserves one further scaling test.
